svg.title: NEWS FEED (FACEBOOK): sketchnote
svg.text: The canonical fan-out problem: build a personalised feed for billions of users in a
Computing the feed on every read means hundreds of
queries per page view, so precompute it when people
Push new post IDs into each follower's feed list in
Redis (fan-out on write); a feed read becomes one
Accounts with millions of followers break fan-out on
write, so pull their posts at read time instead (hybrid).
View feed of followed users' posts, newest first, paginated
2B users; eventual consistency (post appears within ~1 min)
Handle accounts with millions of followers
With ~200 followers each, fan-out on write ≈
posts(id, author_id, content, ts) partitioned by author
feed:{user} = Redis ZSET(ts, post_id), capped at 500
Fan-out on read: look up 200 followees, then their posts, on
every feed load. At 115k feeds/sec that is millions of queries/sec.
Fan-out on write: a new post goes to Kafka; workers
push its ID into every follower's Redis sorted set. A
Celebrity problem: one post to 100M followers means
followers and merge their recent posts at read time.
Hydrate post IDs into content from the posts store,
with a post cache. Cursor pagination on (ts, post_id).
Hybrid. Don't fan out; followers pull celebrity posts at read time and merge.
Only active users, only IDs, capped at 500: 300M × 500 × ~8B ≈ 1.2TB
across a Redis cluster. Inactive users get rebuilt on demand.
Cursor = (ts, post_id) of the last item. Offsets shift as new posts arrive.
An async job backfills the followee's recent posts into the follower's feed.
Fan-out on write for everyone: one celebrity post
means 100M writes and workers hours behind.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
